body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/core ### Is this a regression? Worked in 8 and below ### Description When trying to access `componentFactoryResolver` on an instance of `NgModuleRef` that is not the root module there is an exception thrown:
TypeError: Cannot read property 'get' of undefined

at NgModuleRef$1.get (core.umd.js:24253) at NgModuleRef$1.get [as componentFactoryResolver] (core.umd.js:24257) at new FeatModule (feat-module.ts:8) at Object.FeatModule_Factory [as factory] (feat-module.ts:12) at R3Injector.hydrate (core.umd.js:11505) at R3Injector.get (core.umd.js:11328) at eval (core.umd.js:11268) at Set.forEach () at new R3Injector (core.umd.js:11268) at createInjector (core.umd.js:11233)

The issue is that there is no value in the `_r3Injector` property... it exists only in the root module. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Go to https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-9-abstract-g6cugw?file=src%2Fapp%2Ffeat-module%2Ffeat-module.ts There is a debugger statement in line 22, the issue will throw in line 24. ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 9.0.2
Node: 12.9.1
OS: darwin x64

Angular: 9.0.1
... animations, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, elements
... forms, language-service, platform-browser
... platform-browser-dynamic, platform-server, router
Ivy Workspace: Yes

Also worth noting, that if requesting an injection of `ComponentFactoryResolver` it is totally fine. You get an instance of `ComponentFactoryResolver` that points to it's `NgModuleRef` (`ngModule` prop) and that `NgModuleRef` will **NOT** point to that `ComponentFactoryResolver` we just got... it will throw when trying to access it's `componentFactoryResolver ` property.
